{{Short description|British mathematician}}
[[File:John Gray by William Bond, after Thomas Hudson.jpg|thumb|John Gray FRS]]
'''John Gray''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (died 17 July 1769) was a British mathematician.

As a young man he taught mathematics at [[Marischal College]], later Aberdeen University.<ref name = LA/>

He wrote ''"A Treatise on Gunnery"'', dedicated to the Duke of Argyll and published by William Innys (London) in 1731.<ref name = LA>{{Cite web|url=https://www.liveauctioneers.com/item/5846097_1418-gray-treatise-of-gunnery-1731-mathematics-first|title = Gray TREATISE OF GUNNERY 1731 Mathematics First - Nov 09, 2008 &#124; National Book Auctions in NY}}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Andrew Reid (writer)|Andrew Reid]] and others, he worked to produce a book of abridged ''[[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society]]'' for 1720–1732; which was published by W. Innys and R. Manby in 1732.<ref name=LBSO>{{cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/lbs/person/view/2146649623|title=John Gray Rector of Marischal College|publisher=Legacies of British Slave-ownership|accessdate= 15 December 2017}}</ref>

In March 1732 he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society, his application citation having described him as being of the Navy Office (or [[Navy Board]]), who were responsible for the construction and maintenance of  ships in the Royal Dockyards for the Royal Navy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Persons&dsqPos=36&dsqSearch=%28%28text%29%3D%27gray%27%29|title= Fellow details|publisher= Royal Society|accessdate= 15 December 2017}}</ref>

From 1764 to his death he was [[Rector of the University of Aberdeen|Rector of Marischal College]]. He died at his London home in 1769, having asked to be buried at Petersham next to his wife Elizabeth. He left estates in the West Indies to his nephews and {{convert|1000|acre}} to [[Gray's Inn]] of London.<ref name=LBSO/>
